seven_questions.question: What did you try, and what works now?
seven_questions.answer: Pinned native CUDA builds, separate short reconstruction pretraining, three complete native-flow fine-tunes, strict inference, metrics rechecks and a working recorded browser replay. The generalized build and full-model gate ran in a fresh environment on the same GB10, not a new physical GPU.
seven_questions.assessment: Substantive positive evidence is paired with implemented/executed/validated scope and retained failures.

seven_questions.question: How do NetMamba+ training and inference work?
seven_questions.answer: Reconstruct masked content during pretraining; transfer the released encoder to labeled six-class fine-tuning; use forward/loss/backward/optimizer updates; choose a checkpoint on validation; run fixed saved weights for inference. The short pretraining checkpoint did not initialize the three reported fine-tunes.
seven_questions.assessment: Defines batch, epoch, loss, gradients, optimizer, seed, checkpoint, logits and strict reload, with a sequential worked model path.

seven_questions.question: What data goes in and what comes out?
seven_questions.answer: The two uploads are packet tables with 1,500 payload positions and ttl, total_len, protocol, t_delta, label. Native JSON supplies already assembled packet-byte strings, sizes and intervals; the original transforms create 443 tokens, and the full classifier returns six logits/scores and a class name. Training uses native splits of 8,323 / 1,040 / 1,041 flows, not the uploaded CSVs.
seven_questions.assessment: Explains schema, meaning, grouping/order/header/timing gaps, native class meanings, transformations and unlabeled output; both complete 25-label tables are available in the paper/data guide.

seven_questions.question: What results were actually reproduced versus reported by the paper?
seven_questions.answer: Three full 120-epoch, 7,920-update runs gave 91.26%, 84.05% and 84.63%; mean 86.65% and sample SD 4.00 percentage points on one fixed test split. Paper Table IV NetMamba+ reports 97.50% under different conditions; the gap is not isolated. Repeated inference is an execution check, not new independent accuracy evidence.
seven_questions.assessment: All seed results, actual error counts and statistical meanings are explained; batch/rate/runtime/pretraining differences and optional401/443 notation details are explicit.

seven_questions.question: What could a simple working IDS demo look like?
seven_questions.answer: Show the actual saved-prediction browser replay, then inspect a confidently wrong result: JSON row 635 / display row 0636 predicts RTSP Brute Force at 84.43% although its true category is Other. New inference requires the GPU classifier and native flows. A future live IDS adds verified capture, grouping, features and reviewed alert policy.
seven_questions.assessment: The existing hash-bound browser receipt establishes the working replay and controls. Source includes actual replay imagery and a bounded recorded controls clip. This text audit does not certify the pending v3 encode or claim live capture.

seven_questions.question: How could this map to an AI NPU or SmartNIC?
seven_questions.answer: A proposed NIC/SmartNIC packet and flow path, host orchestration/buffering/policy and supported NPU computation requires an actual preserved-model port. Model-only weight export differs from graph capture; the tested strict graph path failed on a custom CUDA operation. Validate precision, outputs/gradients as relevant, accuracy, full-path latency/throughput and drops.
seven_questions.assessment: Defines hardware roles and separates the measured GB10 model-only timing from a future capture-to-alert system and from the paper online prototype.

seven_questions.question: What is still missing or not working?
seven_questions.answer: Exact paper accuracy/full pretraining; complete inherited checkpoint history; verified live extraction; capture-independent customer validation; calibrated confidence/alert policy; unknown attack detection; CPU/MPS/NPU/native Windows/macOS model backends; additional physical GPU validation; inherited asset terms.
seven_questions.assessment: Missing work is named specifically throughout and repeated near the handoff. Existing positive checks never become universal hardware or customer-accuracy claims.

findings.observation: The broad explanation says an embedding is a learned numerical representation. In this specific model, the byte projection is learned; size and interval base value encodings use parameter-free FixedCosineEmbed, with learned positional and modality additions. Neither reviewed companion explicitly names fixed cosine encoding: paper/data guide section 6, item 4 says original value embedding, while docs/lesson.md line 25 explicitly identifies learned position and modality indicators. Their pinned source links make the exact implementation inspectable.
findings.suggestion: At a future wording pass,define embedding as a numerical vector representation and separately state which parts are learned. No model,result,input-dimension or portability claim changes.
findings.disposition: No tracked edit requested by this bounded audit; nonblocking precision note.

findings.optional_receipt_text: Embedding means representing an input as a numerical vector. Here the byte projection, summary tokens, position vectors and modality indicators are learned. The initial numerical encodings of packet sizes and intervals are fixed sine/cosine functions in the pinned source. The combined tokens still contain learned components. This qualification does not change the 443-token layout, parameter count or measured results.
